canonical_creation.policy: load the same retained canonical creation into every production topology projection without mutating its semantic identities or protected source/audio/provenance meaning

fault_campaign.case: same canonical creation / same authoritative workload
fault_campaign.expected: normalized semantic equality across all supported topology profiles

fault_campaign.case: packet loss plus delayed newer state
fault_campaign.expected: latest valid authority state converges without project rewrite
principal/session/Thing semantics survive while transient transport generation changes
only confirmed checkpoint migrates; epoch increments
state coalesces, reliable events stay bounded, tombstone remove-wins

fault_campaign.case: real Chromium WebRTC disconnect/reconnect and malformed frames
fault_campaign.expected: adapter fails closed and can establish a fresh physical transport without semantic identity rewrite

fault_campaign.case: real Chromium dedicated WSS round trip
fault_campaign.expected: runtime join then bidirectional bounded semantic envelopes over authenticated WSS path

protected_asset_invariant.rule: the complete protected revision is byte-for-byte/deep-value stable across topology projection, delayed delivery, reconnect and host migration; transport state has no field-mixing authority

measurement_policy.claim_boundary: CI-local measurements are mechanism evidence only; no Internet-wide latency, NAT success, throughput or SLO claim

residual_risk: CI cannot represent the full public-Internet NAT/firewall/TURN population; deployment telemetry and later target qualification remain operational evidence.
The gate certifies the selected browser Chromium path plus topology-independent production semantics; other browser/mobile lifecycle breadth requires target-specific qualification.
Transport timing/interpolation/private connection identifiers may differ and are excluded from semantic equivalence.
